title: Arepas with black beans and cheese
skill: A corn dough timed with its fillings

move.title: Griddled, baked, split, and filled
move.body: Arepas are the corn cakes Venezuelans eat every day, split open and stuffed. The dough is just precooked cornmeal, water, and salt, with no leaven. You'll get the black beans simmering first, then shape and griddle the arepas, finish them in the oven, and fill them hot so everything is ready at once.

callback.body: Cornbread baked a batter in a hot skillet. Arepas are a corn dough shaped by hand, browned in a skillet, and finished in the oven.

why.title: Precooked cornmeal
why.body: Masarepa is corn that's been cooked, dried, and ground, so it soaks up warm water in minutes into a smooth dough. Ordinary cornmeal won't form a dough.

why.title: Rest the dough
why.body: Five minutes lets the masarepa drink in all the water. Too dry, the edges crack; too wet, it sticks to your hands. Adjust a spoonful at a time.

why.title: Skillet, then oven
why.body: The skillet browns a crisp crust; the oven cooks the thick middle through without burning it. They're done when they sound hollow when tapped.

why.title: Beans first
why.body: The beans take longest and hold well on low heat. Start them first, and they're hot the moment the arepas come out.

wrong.sign: The edges crack when you flatten them
wrong.fix: The dough is too dry. Knead in a tablespoon of water.

wrong.sign: The dough sticks to your hands
wrong.fix: Wet your hands, or knead in a spoonful of masarepa.

wrong.sign: They're burnt outside and gummy inside
wrong.fix: The skillet was too hot. Use medium heat, and give them the full time in the oven.
Split them while hot with a serrated knife, holding them in a towel.

choices: Corn that's been cooked, dried, and ground
quiz.explain: It forms a dough with warm water.

quiz.q: Why finish arepas in the oven?
choices: To cook the thick middle through without burning the crust
They take longest and hold well

steps.text: Heat the oven to 375°F with a rack in the middle.

Dice the onion and mince the garlic. Soften them in the olive oil in the saucepan over medium heat, then add the cumin, beans, water, and salt. Mash about a third of the beans with the fork, and keep them on low.
steps.look: Thick and creamy, with whole beans.

steps.text: Stir the masarepa and salt into the warm water and 1 tablespoon of the oil in the large bowl. Knead in the bowl for 2 minutes, then rest it.
Divide into 8 balls. Flatten each to a 3½-inch disk, ½ inch thick, smoothing any cracks at the edge with a wet finger.
steps.look: Smooth disks with no cracks around the edge.

steps.text: Heat the rest of the oil in the skillet over medium heat. Cook the arepas in batches until a golden crust forms, then turn and cook the other side.
steps.look: Golden with darker spots on both sides.

steps.text: Move them to the sheet pan and bake until they sound hollow when tapped.
Tap one: it should sound hollow. If it thuds, bake 5 more minutes.
Hold each hot arepa in the towel and split it most of the way with the bread knife. Stuff it with beans and cheese. Turn off the stove and oven.
